claims.text: tools — the capability layer: what tools exist, and what they are cleared for.
claims.why: The module docstring states it is the capability layer; the exports (vet and inventory) align with that purpose.

claims.text: Two modules, one seam: * vet — the gate. Static-only, fail-closed inspection of a skill or an MCP server. Returns findings with evidence, never a score.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the implementation of vet; claims about its behavior (static-only, fail-closed, returns findings with evidence, never a score) cannot be verified from this file alone.

claims.text: inventory — the derived list of every skill and MCP server visible from a project, each carrying its verdict.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the implementation of inventory; claims about its behavior cannot be verified from this file alone.

claims.text: Neither installs, enables, starts nor routes anything. Provisioning and capability routing are separate lanes; routing in particular belongs to provider_router, which already owns lane policy.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain implementation details to confirm that these functions do not install, enable, start, or route. Reference to provider_router is external.

observations.what: The module docstring describes vet and inventory modules and their responsibilities, but the chunk only contains imports and re-exports; no implementation is present.
All symbols listed in __all__ are imported from submodules vet and inventory; no new symbols are defined in this file.
The module docstring references a module 'provider_router' which is not present in this chunk; no path is given.
